The statment in Danish on the parliaments webpage. - - My translation in the bottom of this post.

First my comments on what this means: It is a civic-nationalist move, with hints of ethno-nationalism.

One of the original signatories of the proposition is a member of the conservative party, who was born in Syria and is of Mohammedan-Syrian stock. He is however, currently one of the strongest opponents of further muzzy immigration in parliament, and has repeatedly come out in favour of Trumps 90-day ban, even though he may himself be barred from the US under the ban.

The statement comes after a survey last year found that many 1st, 2nd, and 3rd generation immigrants defined themselves as Pakistani, Palestinian, Turkish and so on, as opposed to Danish. This lead to a debate on whether or not is was acceptable that there were areas where the majority did not define themselves as Danes or follow Danish cultural practices. This is of curse a civic-nationalist point of view, however, there were two statements put forward on the same day, the one that was adopted, and the other, which was dropped.

The main difference being that the dropped one said: "It is Parliaments viewpoint, that integration works best, when the danish culture is bearing in all residential areas in Denmark. There is in that regard a continued need for a focus on democratic child-rearing, equality between the sexes and equal worth between people." Whereas the adopted one simply said: "It is Parliaments viewpoint, that Danes should not be a minority in residential areas in Denmark."

The fact that the explicitly civic version lost to the far more ethno-nationalistic is a great thing, and while the proponents of the adopted statement are still framing it as mainly a civic proposition, the significant differences in wording should be noted. So it's a step in the right direction, tough of course, it is simply a single step in the long struggle. It should also be noted that this is a "Forslag til vedtagelse" which means that it is a statement of intent, or a policy statement, and not an actual law.

 

Adopted statement:

Parliament notes with worry, that there today are areas in Denmark, where the share of immigrants and descendants from non-western nations surpasses 50 pct. It is Parliaments viewpoint, that Danes should not be a minority in residential areas in Denmark. The Government and Parliament have executed a number of tightenings of regulation, that have limited the arrival of asylum-seekers significantly, and that serve to counteract parallel societies. Parliament encourages the Government to continue working with a political goal of reducing the number of asylum-seekers and the number of people who arrive in Denmark under the family-reunion scheme.

 

Dropped statement:

Parliament notes with worry, that there today are areas in Denmark, where the share of immigrants and descendants from non-western nations surpasses 50 pct. It is Parliaments viewpoint, that integration works best, when the danish culture is bearing in all residential areas in Denmark. There is in that regard a continued need for a focus on democratic child-rearing, equality between the sexes and equal worth between people. Parliament has adopted a number of tightenings of regulation, that have limited the arrival of asylum-seekers significantly, and that serve to counteract parallel societies. Parliament encourages the Government to strengthen the work with integration, and securing a low number of asylum-seekers and people arriving in Denmark under the family-reunion scheme.

It was always such an isolated feeling I'd get when staring down the platform when I was going home while I worked in London. I don't believe this pic was taken there (but I could be wrong. The UK overland system is fucking monstrous), but the mood that it invokes is the same.

Being the only person on the platform always made me feel almost a post-apocalyptic sense of loneliness. Like the trains were just rolling on a timer, and I only did my job so that they would keep running. Most nights I would sit in a car all to myself, the slightly feminine voice of the recorded messages being the only source of pseudo-human contact.

When I first started with the nightly commute, I would look for cars with other people in them. I'm very extroverted by nature, and love making new friends. It took less than a week of being nearly attacked by belligerent drunks or out-right psychotics to learn that this simply wasn't a good idea. So I quickly altered my methods to seek out the least populated car that I could find.

I know what you mean, but I always found a kind of quiet beauty in my home city during the very late night, when even the resident petty criminals have gone to sleep. Hearing the distant sound of cars on the nearby highway and the buzzing of the many ventilation fans, it's almost like you can hear the city itself breathing.
